title: Bus two flat 9 in porcelain plates into a deep tub: one hand tips each plate up by its rim so the other can grip it
instruction: Set both plates down in the bus tub, then move both hands clear.
context: Clearing plates is core work in two big restaurant jobs, and a flat 22 mm plate can be gripped only after one hand presses its rim down (about 9 N, 6 to 11 N by foot size) to tip it on its foot ring. Bussers (O*NET 35-9011.00; 542,750 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) have the Core task 'Scrape and stack dirty dishes and carry dishes and other tableware to kitchens for cleaning'; waiters and waitresses (35-3031.00; 2,270,910 US jobs) the Core task of removing dishes from tables. A flat 9 in porcelain plate stands 22 mm high and its rim's underside is 16 mm off the table at the edge, less further in. One hand presses the far side of the rim so the plate tips up on its foot ring and the near rim rises; the other hand closes on the raised rim, lifts the 0.54 kg plate over the tub's 17.6 cm wall and lays it down, the second plate on the first. The solid 15.9 cm well leaves no grip under the rim and the plate swings in the pinch: it must fall under 1.5 cm after the jaws open (demo 1.05 cm).
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, their bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a 120 x 80 cm wood table, 75 cm high, seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table: x forward, y to the robot's left; the layout is the same in every trial. Bus tub: a Cambro 21157CBP Cambox deep bus box, polypropylene, 15 3/16 x 20 3/16 x 6 15/16 in (38.6 x 51.3 x 17.6 cm), its floor 46.3 x 33.6 cm, empty, at the robot's right with its long side along x, spanning x 33 to 84 and y -18 to -56, free to slide on the table. Plates: two Libbey 1502-10235 Empire 9 in (22.9 cm) round porcelain plates, 7/8 in (2.2 cm) tall, about 0.54 kg each (14.35 lb per case of 12, packaging included), empty, face up where two diners left them, centred at (37, -6) and (36, 19). The underside of the rim is 1.6 cm above the table at its edge and 0.5 cm at 7.9 cm from the centre, where the 6 1/4 in (15.9 cm) well ends; the foot ring is 11.6 to 13.2 cm across (design values: the maker gives the diameter, height and well only). The tub weighs about 1.1 kg (a design value). Real trial: the same two plates and tub on a wood or laminate table, the arms as above. To measure drops inside the opaque tub, add a side camera on a tripod at the tub's outer long side, level with the middle of its length, lens 90 cm above the tabletop and 10 cm out from the tub wall, pitched 60 degrees down over the near wall, and a printed scale strip (0 to 17 cm, 5 mm ticks, zero at the inner floor) taped upright inside the far long wall at the middle of its length.
scoring: Terms. In the tub: every sampled point of the plate (its rim's top and edge, and its foot ring) inside the tub, above its floor, below its rim and inside its sloping walls, either way up. Let go: no point of either gripper (fingers, pads, palm, housing) or wrist link within 1 cm of the plate. Set down: once let go, the plate's centre comes to rest no more than 1.5 cm below where it was at the frame the jaws open, measured to where it ends (a plate resting on an open hand has not come to rest; simulator rule: a hand whose finger joint reads past 7.5 mm, a pinched rim 5.8 mm, no longer holds; a plate no closed hand has touched since it last rested is held while a hand is within 1 cm and it moves, as when carried on open fingers). Real trial, on the side camera with the scale strip (setup): at the frame the jaws open and when the plate stops, read its near and far rim heights; the centre drop is the mean of the two rims' drops and must be at most 1.5 cm (with the far rim already resting, the near rim drops at most 3.0 cm). A plate that falls further never counts, even if it is picked up again. 0.4 for each plate in the tub, set down and let go. 1.0: both plates in the tub, set down and let go, and for the last 1 s both grippers and wrist links at least 3 cm from each plate and the tub, and nothing moving more than 1 mm (real trial: nothing visibly moving for the last 1 s; code checks only the plates' and the tub's body origins). 0 if a plate leaves the table (5 cm below the tabletop). Scored on the state at the end of the run.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU. The plates and the tub are free, colliding bodies at real size and mass: each plate's rim is 24 convex segments that follow its section, so a finger can go under its edge, on a solid well and foot; the tub has thin sloping walls. The rim's under-profile and foot ring are design values; friction (porcelain on wood 0.4, on polypropylene 0.4, 0.35 sliding) is estimated. Real trials add a side camera and a scale strip on the tub wall to read the same 1.5 cm centre drop.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (step 1502, 75.1 s); plate fall after release 1.05 cm, limit 1.5 cm
